newsitem.title: USA: Coleman seek to overturn Black & Decker ruling.
newsitem.headline: Coleman seek to overturn Black & Decker ruling.

text.p: Coleman Co Inc said it would try to overturn or reduce a $3.7 million jury verdict awarded Black & Decker Corp in a patent infringement case.
The company said in a statement late on Monday that the decision was returned Friday in Alexandria, Va., in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia.
The verdict involved claims that a prior discontinued Coleman battery-powered light infringed patents held by Black & Decker.
Larry Sanford, an executive vice president of Coleman and its chief legal counsel said, "We have a strong case to set aside this mistaken and excessive verdict."

He added, "The trial court had previously held as a matter of law that Coleman's current product does not directly infringe any Black & Decker patent. In light of that ruling, we believe that a retrial of the matter will result in the complete vindication of Coleman's current product. We are exploring all available options to achieve that objective."
